records.region: Southern Greenland, southern Inland Ice and the exposed-rock/valley belt east and southeast of the Narsarsuaq area.
records.candidate_name_role: No representative natural-river identity established. Narsarsuaq is settlement-based geographic context only.
records.naming_scope_hold_reason: The complete modeled selection is geographically accounted for in the original national terrain cartography, but that source does not identify it as a representative named natural river. The northern ice corridor and lower rock-and-valley passages cannot be assigned one river identity from thematic terrain symbols.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The chosen opening is on southern Inland Ice. FID8925 initially proceeds southeastward, turns west and southwest through the ice/nunatak boundary, enters the exposed-rock belt, and turns south to the junction with FID8926. The entire shorter FID8926 continues south, west and southwest to its own stored ending. The final setting is an inland rock-and-valley corridor in the historical national map, with no independent ordinary-river-mouth or named receiving-water assignment.
records.completion_scope: The actual surviving original national map was visually read at full-sheet, southern-graticule, selected-corridor and enlarged selected-path scales. Both fragments and all89 stored parts are covered without an unviewed geographic interval at this ordinary terrain scale. The final endpoint is that of FID8926. The review does not require exact banks, modern glacier-front position, name-boundary vertices or a surveyed hydrological route.

component_scope_limits: The directly read Narsarsuaq settlement label is geographic context only and is not promoted to a river name.
No glacier, lake, fjord or valley name is inferred for any unlabelled selected section.
A continuous modeled line and its stored terminal classification do not prove a present-day natural river, a through-ice connection or a river mouth.
The national map provides generalized historical terrain correspondence; its geological and ice-contour symbols are not hydraulic evidence.
Candidate null records that this research did not establish a name, not that no local or official name exists.

records.region: Southeastern Córdoba opening near Melo and a long continuation through northern Buenos Aires, south of the Cañada Seca–Rufino–Laguna La Picasa setting, Argentina.
records.material_pending_reason: Substantial selected intervals and the actual endpoint have no usable independent hydrographic correspondence. The retained study and provincial map provide bounded context only; the one targeted independent modelling report could not be obtained. Further broad source expansion was not used to manufacture a name.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selected feature does not follow the complete La Picasa internal canal/reservoir chain and does not end in Laguna La Picasa. The published regional route from its diversion works toward Horquetas and the Salado basin is not sufficient to identify the separate selected southern trace.
records.completion_scope: All 40 selected parts were considered. Retained originals establish the Melo-side regional placement and separation from the La Picasa system, but do not establish the opening, substantial southern lowland through-links or actual terminal.
records.supported_name_scope: No representative river-system name is supported. Nearby La Picasa, Quinto/La Amarga and Horquetas references are contextual and are not transferred to this selected route.

scope_limits: The selected modeled continuity does not establish a natural river, engineered canal or current surface-flow connection.
The source gap does not establish that local channels or depressions are unnamed.
The long route cannot be assigned the nearby lake, basin or river name solely from regional proximity.
Exact present water extent, bank locations, formal name-change vertices, flow direction and operating state are outside the finding.
Distinct supported reach names could later coexist under a representative system identity; a uniform scalar name is not required.

records.geographic_disambiguation: Representative receiving-system identity across the selected Telire–Sixaola corridor; not a scalar name for every selected reach. The initial local reach name is unassigned.
records.completion_scope: All eight selected mainstem fragments, the chosen opening, intervening joins and actual coastal terminal were compared with inspected original cartography at ordinary corridor scale. The finding does not establish exact banks, name-boundary vertices, contemporary hydraulics or formal registry status.
records.supported_name_scope: Representative receiving-system identity across the selected Telire–Sixaola corridor; not a scalar name for every selected reach. The initial local reach name is unassigned.

scope_limits: Telire remains a distinct upper reach; the Sixaola representative candidate does not replace every local name.
The selected southwestern opening is visible, but its exact local hydronym and source vertex are unassigned; the nearby Turi label is not transferred to it.
The published map scales support corridor correspondence, not precise agreement of simplified fragments with individual meanders, banks or current coastal morphology.
No formal-registry check, current flow verification or hydraulic-operational certification was performed.

records.region: Rio Grande do Norte, Brazil; Lajes, Jardim de Angicos, João Câmara, Poço Branco, Taipu, Ceará-Mirim and Extremoz corridor
records.candidate_name_role: Supported middle and lower river-corridor candidate; whole selected-system representative identity remains incomplete.
records.material_pending_reason: The available regional original does not unambiguously establish the selected upper Rio Lajes-area opening and its continuation through the small mapped impoundment near Lajes, or the selected passage through the Poço Branco impoundment and receiving trunk. The two independent studies supplied useful earlier-read prose but no usable original map. These are geographic material gaps, not a completed naming-scope hold or a second access-pending primary status.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Ceará-Mirim in Rio Grande do Norte, north of the separate Potengi/Natal system. The selected downstream corridor is distinct from the southern Rio do Mudo–Rio Guairu–Extremoz lake drainage and the northern Maxaranguape system. No adjacent lake or tributary name is imported into the selected system.
records.completion_scope: All 38 selected parts were considered at ordinary corridor scale. The mapped middle/lower trunk and actual Atlantic ending are supported, while the selected upper opening and two impoundment passages remain incomplete.
records.supported_name_scope: The original state reference map repeatedly labels Rio Ceará-Mirim and depicts its continuation east through Taipu and Ceará-Mirim, then southeast to the Atlantic. Rio Lajes is separately labelled beside the selected western approach; distinct reach names are retained rather than forced into a scalar name.

scope_limits: The opening is a selected endpoint, not a verified natural spring. Its river/impoundment join is not established by general Lajes headwater prose.
The two mapped water bodies along the upper and middle corridor lack complete selected through-correspondence; only the Poço Branco setting has an independently read reservoir name.
Regional map generalization supports trunk and coastal setting, without proving exact channel branches, bank vertices, present water levels, current flow or managed operations.
The2017 article's inconsistent S11 longitude is excluded from terminal positioning; the original map and study-area destination support the broad ending.
No accepted whole-feature scalar name, Korean name or formal registry verification is established.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
